_about: Water (1) + cyclohexane (2): heterogeneous (two-liquid) azeotrope at 101.325 kPa, as tabulated in the Wikipedia 'Azeotrope tables' article. Row as printed: azeotrope boiling point in degC and composition in weight percent of cyclohexane (the second component).

source.citation: Azeotrope tables, Wikipedia, table 'binary azeotropes of water', row cyclohexane (colour code 'CRC only'); values from the CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics (44th ed., 1962)
source.access: Open (CC BY-SA text; handbook values). Secondary compilation, the same source as validation/data/azeotropes_101kPa.json.
source.tables: Binary azeotropes of water, row 'cyclohexane': b.p. of component 80.7 degC, b.p. of mixture 69.8 degC, % by weight 91.5 (U 99.99, L 0.01), specific gravity U 0.780, L 1.00

notes: Old handbook value (1962), no uncertainty given. 91.5 wt % cyclohexane is the overall (vapour) azeotrope composition; the layers (U 99.99, L 0.01 wt %) are not used. Not fitted: an independent check of the water + cyclohexane parameters, which are fitted to mutual solubilities only (validation/python/fit_parameters.py converts the weight percent to a vapour mole fraction with the molar masses in src/data/components.json).
